publications.title: European Supervisory Authorities set priorities for 2027
publications.summary: European Supervisory Authorities set priorities for 2027 13 October 2026 Joint Committee The Joint Committee of the European Supervisory Authorities (EBA, EIOPA and ESMA – the ESAs) published today its Annual Work Programme for 2027 , setting out its priorities for addressing cross-sectoral risks and strengthening coordination across the European Union's financial sector. In 2027, the Joint Committee will focus on areas where cooperation among the three ESAs is essential to support financial stability, consumer protection and effective supervision. Key priorities include digital operational resilience, technological innovation, sustainable finance, securitisation and cross-sectoral risk monitoring. publications.summary: The FCA has conducted a major operation to disrupt a suspected organised criminal group for engaging in insider dealing and money laundering. publications.summary: Two people who worked at financial advice firms have pleaded guilty to fraud after 4 clients lost £2m. Nelson has also admitted a money laundering offence after money was withdrawn from the firms, which she used to fund her extravagant lifestyle.Therese Chambers, executive director of enforcement and market oversight at the FCA, said:'This was a serious breach of trust. publications.summary: The Upper Tribunal has confirmed it will hear the legal challenges to our motor finance compensation scheme between 16 to 26 February 2027. publications.title: ESMA promotes clarity in claims on impact and transition
publications.summary: ESMA promotes clarity in claims on impact and transition 12 October 2026 Sustainable finance The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA), the EU’s financial markets regulator and supervisor, has published two additional thematic notes on sustainability-related claims. Impact claims This thematic note examines positive impact claims made through funds and bonds. Market participants understand positive environmental or social impact differently and attach different levels of ambition to their impact claims. Therefore, they are encouraged to explain clearly what difference they expect to make, how they aim to generate positive impact and how they will measure results, so that investors receive clear and balanced information. publications.title: Basel Committee finds Australia, Japan, Korea, Switzerland compliant, and Canada, United Kingdom largely compliant with its leverage ratio framework
publications.summary: The Basel Committee has published assessment reports on the implementation of its leverage ratio framework (LEV) in Australia, Canada, Japan, Korea, Switzerland and the United Kingdom. Australia, Japan, Korea and Switzerland are assessed as compliant; Canada and the United Kingdom are assessed as largely compliant. This publication concludes the first round of multi-jurisdictional assessments of the leverage ratio.

publications.title: Are stablecoins and bank deposits substitutes?
publications.summary: We test whether stablecoins and bank deposits act as substitutes by estimating the semi-elasticity of stablecoin market capitalization with respect to deposit rate changes. Using local projections fit to weekly U.S. data from January 2019 to June 2025, we find that deposit rate increases predict slower stablecoin growth. To address endogeneity, we exploit a nonlinearity in deposit rate pass-through. Whereas other money market rates track the federal funds rate roughly linearly, banksreprice deposits more aggressively once it exceeds approximately 3%.
